evals.name: customer-repository
evals.expected_output: A small working repository implementation with focused MUnit tests. The required lookups work without exposing mutable backing state or unrelated public access paths.
expectations: Lookup by ID returns the matching customer and None for a missing ID.
Lookup by email is exact and returns None for missing or differently-cased email addresses.
Active customers are filtered by region and status, preserve input order, and a missing region returns an empty list.
CustomerRepository exposes exactly findById, findByEmail, and activeByRegion.
InMemoryCustomerRepository exposes no public mutable state, including constructor fields.
Helpers are private or protected, with no public all, records, or generic query escape hatch.
No public method or value exposes a mutable collection type.
The submission includes focused MUnit coverage for all three required operations.
The solution is proportional to three in-memory lookups and adds no unrelated architecture.
The solution adds no DTO, identifier, result, or mapping wrapper without a concrete benefit.

evals.name: repository-with-callers
evals.prompt:
Add email lookup support to the in-memory customer repository in the starter application. Match email addresses exactly, return the first customer in input order when multiple customers share an email, and return None when there is no match.

Keep the application's existing lookup and export behavior working. Add MUnit regression coverage and run `scala-cli test . --server=false`.
evals.expected_output: A focused email lookup enhancement that preserves the immutable snapshot used by the application's export consumer, hides mutable backing state, and narrows unused prototype helpers.
expectations: Email lookup is exact, returns the first match, and represents absence with None.
Existing ID lookup behavior remains compatible.
The immutable snapshot API and export consumer preserve all customers in input order.
The repository preserves findById, findByEmail, and the caller-required snapshot without extra public helpers.
The implementation exposes no public mutable backing state, including constructor fields.
Public repository members expose no mutable collections.
The submission adds executable MUnit email lookup assertions.
The lookup enhancement stays proportional and adds no unrelated architecture or unjustified wrappers.

evals.name: teacher-course-ids
evals.prompt:
Fix the teacher lookup bug in this application. Looking up user 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001 in course 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000002 currently misses their membership, or returns the wrong teacher when the reversed membership exists. Repeated lookups must stay isolated by both user and course.

Keep the existing URL, roster, persistence, directory, and invalid/missing lookup behavior working. This is an internal application; update affected signatures and callers as needed. Add MUnit regression coverage and run `scala-cli test . --server=false`.
evals.expected_output: A focused lookup correction with regression coverage and compatible consumers. The architectural quality assessment separately checks whether the solution prevents the demonstrated identifier mix-up with distinct types across the lookup and cache.
expectations: HTTP lookup distinguishes user and course IDs even when the reversed membership exists.
Cached lookups remain isolated by both user and course, including reversed pairs.
The roster consumer preserves course order, missing memberships, and UUID inputs.
HTTP UUID strings, invalid-identifier errors, and missing-teacher responses remain compatible.
Service and repository lookup APIs reject swapped and raw identifiers at compile time.
Existing directory consumers and UUID persistence records retain their behavior.
Distinct user and course types protect the lookup and cache without an unrelated identifier migration.
The submission adds focused MUnit regression coverage with distinct user and course UUIDs.

evals.name: public-profile-dto
evals.prompt: Add the member-since year to the public profile page. The existing UI is in frontend/PublicProfile.vue; have the profile endpoint return memberSinceYear as a JSON integer derived from the account creation date, and show it below the bio. Preserve the existing profile display, missing-avatar behavior, and invalid/missing-profile responses. The internal account backup must still round trip. Add MUnit regression coverage and run `scala-cli test . --server=false`.
evals.expected_output: The page displays the correct member-since year. Behavioral checks cover the new field and existing consumers; independent safety and architecture checks assess whether the agent recognizes the differing public/private contracts and introduces an explicit public projection without being prompted to do so.
expectations: Successful public profiles preserve displayed fields and include the correct integer memberSinceYear.
Profiles with no avatar retain the avatarUrl key with a JSON null value.
Public responses expose no email, password hash, refresh token, admin flag, or account timestamp.
Profile text is serialized as JSON safely, including quotes, newlines, Unicode, and empty values.
Invalid and missing profile identifiers retain JSON errors, status codes, and content type.
Persistence and the internal backup round trip retain every account field after a public profile read.
The public response has an explicit transport representation independent of the internal account record, using the existing JSON codec.
The change stays focused on the profile boundary and preserves the existing repository and backup responsibilities.
The submission adds executable MUnit coverage that would catch internal account fields leaking into a public response.

evals.name: invitation-preview
evals.prompt:
Add the pending-invitation preview in InvitationMessages.pendingPreview for the classroom invitation screen.

Show the cleaned course title followed by the number of pending invitations and their email addresses. Include only invitations that have not been accepted; normalize email addresses with the existing rules, remove duplicates, sort alphabetically, and join with a comma and space. Use these display forms:
- Scala club: no pending invitations
- Scala club: 1 pending invitation: ada@example.com
- Scala club: 2 pending invitations: ada@example.com, grace@example.com

Keep the existing accepted summary and CSV export working. Add MUnit coverage for the preview and run scala-cli test . --server=false.
evals.expected_output: A working preview with focused new coverage, readable new expressions, and no changes to working methods, existing tests, or formatting.
expectations: Pending previews normalize, deduplicate, and sort only unaccepted email addresses.
Empty and singular previews preserve the requested display contract.
Existing working methods retain their implementation and formatting.
Existing test bodies are preserved and project configuration is unchanged.
New or necessarily changed production expressions keep conditionals outside interpolation.
New or necessarily changed production expressions avoid long receiver chains and nested pipelines.
